overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the March 18 meeting was cancelled, no secret meeting occurred, and the later memo was not minutes. It reminded the committee of its complaint-response deadline.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee held a secret meeting on March 18 without proper notice after announcing it had been cancelled.
allegations.key_passage: The March 18 meeting was, in fact, cancelled.

allegations.summary: A memo the committee filed with the Town Clerk about an abandoned April 21 meeting was examined to see whether it served as minutes of a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: This memo was never intended to constitute official minutes of a Committee meeting, and, indeed, no meeting took place on April 21.

allegations.summary: The committee did not respond to the Open Meeting Law complaint within the 14-business-day period required by law.
allegations.key_passage: We remind the Committee of its obligation to respond to Open Meeting Law complaints.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
